raw_response:
I am old now, and with only two people at home, I cannot spread myself too thin. I will still keep the wheat-maize land as the main thing, because that is the steady way here, and I will keep only a smaller piece in scallion for cash. Wheat and maize fill the stomach and bring steady money; scallion can sell for better cash, but it needs more hand work, more watching, and more spending. I do not read books, so I do it the way I have seen over the years: follow the season, watch the field color, watch the water, and spend carefully but not so little that the crop goes weak.

Since it is April 17, 2026, the wheat for this summer was already sown last October, so for wheat my job now is mainly water once more if the ground turns dry, add a last bit of urea if the leaves look pale, then harvest in June and hurry to put maize in. Maize I will plant right after wheat on the same land, because delaying even a few days can cut yield. Scallion I will keep on a smaller separate block, because it brings cash but is tiring for two old people.
